content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or high historical values.
- Underestimates prices in low-range historical contexts, particularly when recent values are declining or near support levels.
- Shows persistent lag in adjusting to downward trends; forecasts often remain elevated longer than actual price drops.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves, then fails to correct downward quickly — exhibits “overshoot and lag” behavior.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model tends to hold high forecasts longer than actual price reversion to mean.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days after a spike, then gradually adjust — but often too slowly.
- When history includes multiple consecutive high values, model tends to overfit the recent trend and fails to anticipate eventual pullback.
- In low volatility periods, model underestimates the true price range, especially when true values are near recent lows.
